prompts: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: replacement complete-body animation sprite sheet for a Chinese side-scrolling Wukong game. Input image 1 is the edit target and identity/style reference: retain exactly the same adult Sun Wukong face, monkey anatomy, gold armor, teal trousers, red sash and long red head ribbons, golden boots and ONE continuous golden staff. Edit the sheet into a new EIGHT-FRAME GROUND LOW STAFF SWEEP animation, exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, reading left to right. Landscape 1536 x 1024 if possible. Transparent alpha background. No extra frames. Each cell contains ONE complete connected body and both legs, boots and staff, with clear empty padding between every cell. Grounded side view facing RIGHT throughout, consistent head/torso size and staff thickness across all eight frames. This is a real martial staff sequence, not a gun aiming pose and not a jump. Keep feet firmly registered at each cell's shared floor baseline; do not shrink the character when crouching. Ordered poses: 1 upright diagonal guard, 2 visibly bend both knees and lower pelvis while winding staff back, 3 deep wide low lunge with rear leg stretched and front knee bent, torso leaned forward, both hands low, 4 forcefully sweep the staff FORWARD almost horizontally at ankle/shin height while the body remains very low, 5 strong low sweeping follow-through with torso turned and weight transferred to the forward leg, 6 low reverse sweep/recovery with both boots touching the ground, 7 rise naturally back into guard, 8 same upright diagonal guard as frame 1. Essential: frames 3,4,5 must clearly be much lower in stance than the standing frames, with a true ankle/shin-height staff sweep and both hands visibly gripping the SAME shaft. Knees and ankles stay anatomically coherent. Staff, hair and cloth fit completely within each cell and do not touch neighbouring cells. Preserve painterly illustrated game style and detailed armor of the reference. Avoid detached limbs, duplicated staff ends, extra arms, flattened bodies, rotated whole sprites, motion streaks, text, numbers, labels, backgrounds, panels, ground, shadows, lightning, blood or impact effects. Actual transparent pixels outside figures.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this eight-frame Wukong sprite sheet only to correct the staff grip/angle in the five middle poses (frames 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 reading left-to-right). Preserve the same complete connected bodies, face, outfit, size, four-column two-row layout and all eight poses. Keep frames 1,7,8 as the diagonal guard/recovery. In frames 2-6, the staff MUST be a single perfectly straight HORIZONTAL pole in the side-view image, with both ends at the SAME vertical height (within 3 degrees), not pointing downward. Move the gripping hands and forearms naturally to grip that horizontal pole while preserving the rest of the body's low martial stance. Frame 2 winds a horizontal pole across the lower waist; frames 3,4,5 sweep the horizontal pole at shin/ankle height during a deep lunge; frame 6 recovers a horizontal waist-height pole before rising. This is required so that a long game staff can extend along that axis without going through the ground. Keep both boots touching each cell's same baseline, same head size and detailed gold armor, teal trousers, red ribbons and monkey tail. Clear empty gaps between all eight complete figures; no limbs or poles touch neighbouring figures. Same 1536 by 1024 transparent-alpha image, no background, no text, no shadows or effects. Fully transparent pixels outside the figures. Do not crop, flatten, duplicate, rotate the whole body, or change the character identity.
